blockers.title: Stale-release pinning silently bypassed on session-cache hits (new, found by this assessment)

evidence.root_cause: SessionCache.key omits expected_releases (harness/search/orchestrator.py:259-266) while cache.put stores only failure-free results (harness/search/orchestrator.py:406)

blockers.why_blocker: Correctness defect in a fail-closed safety path: a client that pins an old release can be served newer decision data with partial_result false and no failure, contradicting the recorded action 'stale decision data never silently used'.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Include a canonical hash of expected_releases among the SessionCache.key inputs, then add a regression test for the unpinned-then-pinned-stale sequence asserting release_mismatch and partial_result true on a cache hit.

blockers.title: Provenance unresolvable end-to-end (R11.2) - resolver reads the wrong field path

evidence.actual_location: entry.source.document_sha256 (with page_1based, figure_index, locator, caption, source_artifact)

blockers.why_blocker: A ranked number cannot be navigated to its datasheet page through the integrated path even though the underlying evidence rows exist in the M5 index. R11 requires provenance backfill completion before production.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Extend resolve_evidence_refs to read source.document_sha256 / source.page_1based / source.locator in addition to the top-level keys, plus a regression test asserting documents non-empty and unresolved_evidence_ids empty for a supported journey. Keep the 5 unresolved stems and pageless units discovery-only.

blockers.title: Per-request latency dominated by an uncached, uninstrumented release fingerprint (R11.3 cohort caching is necessary but not sufficient)

evidence.root_cause: meta.policy_identity is 'hybrid-v1.1(...)' while DISCOVERY-01 serves 'discovery01-v1(...)', so the cached release never matches and all 443,604 unit rows are re-fingerprinted per request; a read-only serving connection cannot persist the result
evidence.cohort_cache: in-memory LRU max_entries=64, lost on restart

blockers.why_blocker: R11 lists cohort caching as a production criterion. Measured behaviour is worse than the cohort lever implies: even a full session-cache hit costs ~2.9s because the fingerprint is recomputed every request, and the served discovery release id is never persisted anywhere.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Make the release cache policy-identity-keyed (or memoise release_view per serving process with invalidation on index mutation) so the discovery fingerprint is computed once; then add persistent cohort caching. Do not simply prime the single-row meta cache: that would overwrite the hybrid search path's policy identity and invalidate its release.

blockers.title: Auth policy not production-grade beyond localhost (R11.4)
blockers.why_blocker: R11 requires an auth policy before cross-machine production. The session route serves decisions with no credentials, M4 auth fails OPEN when ENGINEERING_DECISIONS_TOKEN is unset, and M4 lacks the non-local bind guard M5 has - one host variable away from an unauthenticated public decisions endpoint.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Fail closed: refuse to start (or refuse non-local bind) when no token is configured; add the SEARCH_ALLOW_REMOTE-style guard to M4; use hmac.compare_digest. Then define per-client credentials, TLS and an audit trail before any non-localhost exposure.

blockers.title: Family grain not propagated to the catalog (R11.5) and this branch's records contradict the live data
blockers.why_blocker: R11.5 requires family-grain population. The admissions exist and are owner-approved in the live identity store, but the catalog that discovery serves from still has no family values, 15 series->family links remain undecided, and this branch's documents assert the opposite of the live data - so promotion could be decided from paperwork that contradicts the databases.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Propagate verified memberships into parts.family (or serve family grain from the identity store), decide the 15 outstanding series->family links, then reconcile the branch (merge/rebase discovery/01-facet-decision-integration or re-issue the admission records here) and correct the four stale documents.

blockers.title: M4 ranking population and M5 discovery cohort are disjoint; the crosswalk is a test fixture (new, found by this assessment)
blockers.why_blocker: The session returns a 1,577-part cohort with facets and guidance alongside a ranking of parts that cohort does not contain and the catalog cannot identify. Facet narrowing cannot influence the ranking, no ranked part links to catalog identity or family, and the retained unknown has part null. Disclosed via cohort_state counts, but never stated plainly, so a consumer can read the ranking as covering the cohort.
blockers.smallest_safe_remediation: Replace the fixture with a crosswalk generated from the identity store, and resolve the population mismatch as an owner data-scope decision: extend M4 curve extraction to catalog (Infineon) parts, or admit the M4 bundle's TI/Vishay parts into catalog and identity. In the meantime add an explicit 'ranked parts are outside the discovery cohort' disclosure to every response.

state_hygiene_note: Catalog and search index were opened read-only (mode=ro) throughout; no flag, release, admission or index mutation was performed. The serving path performs one by-design write: a content-addressed identity snapshot row in facet_identity.db.releases (idempotent, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), inherent to exercising the integrated endpoint. All three databases are WAL-mode; catalog.db mtime moved with a 0-byte WAL and unchanged size (WAL/shared-memory housekeeping, not an assessment write).

gate_evaluation.release_identity_durable_and_observable: PARTIAL - deterministic, observable per response and stable across restart, but never persisted for the discovery policy and not equal to the db-cached release
gate_evaluation.failure_modes_fail_closed: PARTIAL - correct on cache miss, M4 failure and no-comparison paths; release pinning fails open on cache hits (B3); M4 auth fails open with no token configured (B4)

verdict_rationale: Three of the four repository-defined R11 criteria are open outright (provenance completion, cohort caching, auth policy) and the fourth - admission decisions - is satisfied in the live identity store (626 family + 237 series verified with recorded owner approvals) but not propagated to the catalog (parts.family 0/1882), not present in this branch, and contradicted by four of this branch's documents. This assessment also found three items not previously recorded: the stale-pin cache bypass (B3), the uncached per-request release fingerprint that dominates latency (B5), and the disjoint M4/M5 part populations served through a test-fixture crosswalk (B6). Parity being green is necessary but not sufficient. Fix order puts the two small correctness/latency defects first (B3, B2), then latency (B5), then auth (B4), then catalog propagation and branch reconciliation (B1), leaving B6 last because it requires an owner data-scope decision.
